authoritative_principles: NEVER fabricate numbers (material, labour, market prices, margins).
Deterministic Python Pricing Engine is the source of financial truth.
Non-negotiable seller price floor is a strict business constraint.
Tactical reasoning powered by openai/gpt-oss-120b & 20b with Python rule guardrails.

conversations.title: Conversation 1 — Seller Questions the Recommended Price

turns.speaker: seller
turns.message: Why are you suggesting ₹500 per basket? I think ₹400 is enough.
turns.agent_reasoning: Explain that the recommendation is rooted strictly in production data and total unit cost.
turns.expected_response: The ₹500 recommendation is based on your production data. Your estimated cost is approximately ₹342 per basket.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.agent_reasoning: Break down itemized production costs: material ₹61.67, 5 workers @ ₹400/day for 3 days (₹200/unit), rent ₹50, energy ₹20, transport ₹10.
turns.expected_response: It includes Material cost, ₹400/day labour for 5 workers, 3 production days, Workshop rental, Electricity, and Transportation across your 30 baskets batch.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.message: What happens if I sell it for ₹400?
turns.agent_reasoning: Explain that ₹400 leaves only ₹58 profit per unit, which violates the 25% target margin and leaves no buffer for cost variance.
turns.expected_response: ₹400 would still generate approximately ₹58 per basket above the production cost, but it is below your configured target margin and may not adequately cover cost variations.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.agent_reasoning: Clarify that ₹500 is the seller's minimum acceptable price floor provided during onboarding.
turns.expected_response: ₹500 is being used as the minimum acceptable selling price you provided. I recommend keeping the selling range around ₹500–₹520, subject to current market references.

conversations.title: Conversation 2 — Seller Wants to Increase the Price

turns.speaker: seller
turns.message: I want to sell this basket for ₹700.
turns.agent_reasoning: Compare against market reference range (₹450-₹550) and explain why ₹700 is above market.
turns.expected_response: You can choose ₹700, but the current market reference and production data do not strongly support that price.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.agent_reasoning: Explain that unit cost is ₹342 and comparable products range from ₹450-₹550.
turns.expected_response: Your estimated production cost is ₹342 per basket, while the available comparable-product range is approximately ₹450–₹550. ₹700 is therefore significantly above the observed market range.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.agent_reasoning: Acknowledge craftsmanship premium and suggest a balanced range (₹550-₹600) instead of jump to ₹700.
turns.expected_response: That can justify a premium. If your product has verified differentiating factors such as premium bamboo, additional craftsmanship, customization, or larger dimensions, we can factor those into the pricing analysis.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.message: It takes 3 days and 5 workers to make it.
turns.agent_reasoning: Clarify that time and worker wages are already in the base ₹342 cost. Reiterate ₹550-₹600 range.
turns.expected_response: That information is already included in the production-cost calculation. I would recommend ₹550–₹600 if the product differentiation is supported, rather than automatically setting ₹700.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.agent_reasoning: Validate ₹580 >= ₹500 floor. Record as seller-selected price.
turns.expected_response: ₹580 is above your minimum price of ₹500. I can record ₹580 as your seller-selected price.

conversations.title: Conversation 3 — Buyer Negotiation Through the Agent

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.message: I want 100 baskets. Can I get them for ₹450 each?
turns.expected_response: The seller's current minimum acceptable price is ₹500 per basket, so I cannot confirm ₹450.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.message: Why is it ₹500? I'm ordering 100 pieces.
turns.expected_response: The seller's estimated production cost is approximately ₹342 per basket. The ₹500 minimum also accounts for the seller's configured margin and production-related costs.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.message: Since I'm buying 100, ask the seller for a discount.
turns.expected_response: I can request a bulk-order consideration. The seller's price floor is ₹500, so any accepted offer must remain at or above ₹500 unless the seller explicitly changes that floor.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.expected_response: ₹500 meets the seller's current minimum price. I can submit 100 × ₹500 = ₹50,000 as the proposed order value.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.expected_response: The seller has accepted the offer. Order Status: NEGOTIATION -> ACCEPTED.
